Refutations propagated:
- H3 and its children: E004, E010, E011 show the run is energy-bound, so overhead cuts don't pay.
- H1.4: augmentation (E008).
- H2.3: selective backprop (E012).
- H6.1: LR to zero (E015).
- H2.1.2 (E013) and H2.5/H2.5.1 (E014).

Corrections:
- H2.5 was rewritten: E006 never used random-resized crop, so only the 2x2 final-map half was tested (and refuted), and the crop half is retired as moot. H2.1's wording was fixed the same way.
- H2.6 was corrected: group 2, not group 1, carries ~48% of the FLOPs.
- H1.5.1 is supported by E007.
- H5 was trimmed to 0.55; it rests on external evidence only.
- H6 was narrowed to regime-specific levers.

New nodes:
- N1/N1a: total epochs matter more than the 32 px share; a 24 px epoch substitutes for most of a 32 px one.
- N2: 24->32 two-stage schedule at 9.5-10 epochs, with no 28 px phase. This is the next run to do.
- N3/N3a: resolutions below 24 px.
- N4/N4a: smaller batches for accuracy at equal time.
- N5/N5a: tanh-approximate GELU.
- N6: epoch slope above 8.5 epochs.

Open housekeeping:
- Report E013/E016's augmentation hashes to close H2.1.3.
- E006's results.tsv description wrongly says random-resized crop; per its implementation note, it used flip + translate followed by an antialiased downsample."}

updates.statement: Sample efficiency at full resolution drives the score. A1a (airbench96-style: frozen 2x2 whitening stem, 3-conv groups 128/384/576 with dirac init and residuals, SGD-Nesterov lr 9 with BN biases at 64x LR, LS 0.3, lookahead-EMA, alternating flip + translate 2) reaches >=75.3% at 8.5 epochs (E001/E002: 0.7549, 7.22 s), but its margin is thin: neutral perturbations land at 0.752-0.753 (E004, E011). The local slope is steep, ~1 pp/epoch at 8.0-8.5 (E007). At 8.0 full-res epochs, zero-cost augmentation, LS and LR-endpoint tweaks showed no effect >=0.3 pp (E008, E009, E015). New accuracy slack must therefore come from cheaper epochs, more updates or capacity per FLOP, not from retuning the reference.

Still supported by E001/E002, but both neutral perturbations (E004 0.7529, E011 0.7520) fell below 0.753, so the starting point is feasible on seeds 0-2 yet probably a favourable draw.

Evidence: E007~ E008-. With jitter the 8.0-epoch accuracy was 0.7486, which is <0.753 and below the control's 0.7502. The prediction failed by ~0.45 pp, well beyond the ~0.25 pp noise relative to the bar.

Measured epoch cost is stepwise in resolution (24 px 57%, 26 px 75%, 28 px 79%, 30 px 95% of a 32 px epoch; E013), so the levers are 24 px (or lower) phases and narrower high-FLOP layers, with the saved time reinvested in more total epochs.

The reference ablations show capacity is costly to remove on CIFAR-100, so the cut must be paired with the extra epochs it buys.

updates.statement: At 8.5 full-res epochs, group 2 width 384->320 cuts time by >=8% with a 3-seed accuracy loss <=0.4 pp versus A1a, i.e. a better exchange rate than cutting epochs (0.08 pp per 1%).
updates.reason: Retargeted to the group with the largest FLOP share. The bar is tied to the measured full-res epoch-cut exchange rate.

Evidence: E004- E010- E011-. Shrinking prepare (time conserved), halving the step count (0% time) and fusing the optimizer (-0.4%) all failed. On this power-capped GPU, overhead is hidden at 32 px. It could reopen only if H2.4.1 shows low-res phases below the cap.
Evidence: E011-. Fused optimizer plus compiled step: -0.4% time (<2%). Fable's CIFAR-10 experience agrees: CUDA graphs plus foreach gave ~2% at most.
Evidence: E011-. -0.4% time, accuracy 0.7520 (-0.3 pp).
Evidence: E010-. bs 2000 halved the steps with no time change, and accuracy fell 0.81 pp. The opposite direction (smaller batches for accuracy) is a new node under H1.
Evidence: E010-. Time -0.1% (needed >=3%); accuracy 0.7468.

updates.statement: Accuracy and timing noise set the usable margin. Accuracy is deterministic per seed (E002), so the relevant noise is how much the 3-seed mean moves under small, neutral recipe changes: ~0.4 pp per seed and ~0.25 pp on the mean (E004, E005, E011). Both neutral perturbations of A1a landed below its seeds 0-2 mean (0.7529, 0.7520), so A1a's perturbation-averaged mean is ~0.753 and 0.7549 is likely a favourable draw. A new tip needs a 3-seed mean >=0.756 or extra-seed confirmation (seeds 3-10 mean >=0.751). Time noise is ~0.1-0.5%, so time differences >=1% are resolvable.
updates.reason: Evidence: E002+ E004 E011. Adds the observation that perturbations land below the baseline, plus the acceptance rule.
E004 and E011 (neutral perturbations) moved the A1a mean down by 0.2-0.3 pp, consistent with this claim; H4.2.1 and H4.2.2 are not yet run.
Confidence lowered: two perturbations suggest A1a's typical mean is ~0.753, so seeds 3-10 could well land below 0.751. Run this before declaring any new tip.
Direct external evidence on this exact task (the reference PR: 'Muon lost to SGD at every size' on CIFAR-100), but no local run. Slightly lowered from 0.65 per the review. Low priority to test.
Same external support as H5, no local run.

updates.statement: Zero-time-cost accuracy levers can buy 0.2-0.5 pp of slack to spend on epoch or resolution cuts. At 8.0 full-res epochs, LR-to-zero, LS 0.2 and brightness/contrast jitter showed no effect >=0.3 pp (E008, E009, E015; each a single run within noise). What remains is regime-specific: BN recalibration at 32 px after low-res phases, and LS/EMA-horizon retuning once a progressive recipe is the tip.
updates.reason: Evidence: E008- E009- E015-. Each null is within noise, so the node is narrowed and down-weighted rather than closed.

Evidence: E015-. Decaying to 0 gave -0.16 pp vs the control (needed >=+0.2 pp). With the cubic-ramped lookahead EMA already averaging late iterates, the 0.07x floor is fine. Single run, but the result is on the wrong side of the predicted direction.
Evidence: E015-. 0.7486 vs control 0.7502; time unchanged.

updates.statement: On a 24->32 progressive schedule, a forward-only BN re-estimation pass at 32 px over ~10% of an epoch of augmented training data, run inside train, raises 3-seed accuracy by >=0.2 pp at <2% time cost.
updates.reason: Retargeted to the 24->32 schedule that is now the main line. Also note BN momentum 0.4 already adapts quickly in the 32 px tail, which may make this a no-op.

new.statement: Accuracy at a fixed short budget tracks total training epochs/steps far more than the share spent at 32 px: a 24 px epoch carries most of a 32 px epoch's accuracy value at 57% of its cost. Evidence pattern: E013 put 1.8x more epochs at 32 px than E006 yet gained only +0.26 pp, and E006 (9 ep, mostly low-res) is only 0.22 pp behind 8 full-res epochs (E007) while costing 0.92 s less.
With the E006 operator and no 28 px phase, 6@24 + 4@32 px (10 epochs, ~6.5 s by the cost table) gives >=0.3 pp higher 3-seed accuracy than 4@24 + 5@32 px (9 epochs, ~6.4 s), with time within +2%.

A two-stage 24->32 px schedule (E006 operator, no 28 px phase) at 9.5-10 total epochs, with 24 px for <=60% of steps and LR/EMA rescaled to the step count, gives 3-seed accuracy >=0.753 at time <=6.6 s (>=8.6% below A1a). Predicted time = per-epoch cost table (24 px 0.485 s, 32 px 0.848 s) + ~0.2 s overhead.

Resolutions below 24 px (16-20 px) are disproportionately cheap, because the cost curve is stepwise in post-pool map sizes. Final-map geometry does not matter (E014), so a short first phase at <=20 px costs little accuracy and frees budget for more 24/32 px epochs.

A compiled per-epoch cost measurement (2 epochs each, no scored run) shows a 20 px epoch <=0.45x and a 16 px epoch <=0.35x the cost of a 32 px epoch. A 16->24->32 schedule (e.g. 2@16 + 4@24 + 4@32) then reaches >=0.753 at <=6.3 s.

On this energy-bound GPU the optimizer step count is nearly free in time (E010: half the steps, same time), and more updates help accuracy at a fixed epoch budget (E010: bs 2000 cost -0.81 pp). Smaller batches (512-768) should therefore buy accuracy at roughly equal time, unless smaller GEMMs lose efficiency (E012).
A1a at bs 768 (LR/wd/EMA scaled by the same kilostep rule as E010, in reverse), 8.5 epochs, gives a 3-seed accuracy >=0.757 with time within +3% of 7.22 s.

GELU's exact erf costs measurable energy in the fused BN+activation kernels (E003: SiLU saved 2.2%). A cheaper GELU approximation (tanh or polynomial) keeps GELU's accuracy advantage while saving part of that cost, and stacks on any schedule.
Replacing exact GELU with GELU(approximate='tanh') on A1a reduces time by >=1% with a 3-seed accuracy within 0.25 pp of A1a (>=0.7525).

Full-res A1a at 9.0 epochs (LR/EMA rescaled to the step count) gains <=0.3 pp over 8.5 epochs (3-seed accuracy <=0.758) at 7.6-7.7 s, i.e. the slope above 8.5 epochs is less than half the measured 8.0->8.5 slope.

structured_output.summary:
Revision after E000-E016. The only feasible point is still A1a (0.7549, 7.22 s), and two neutral perturbations of it (E004, E011) landed at 0.752-0.753, so H1.1.1 is down-weighted and H4 now carries an acceptance rule: a new tip needs a 3-seed mean >=0.756 or a seeds 3-10 confirmation.

Refutations propagated:
- H3 and its children: E004, E010, E011 show the run is energy-bound, so overhead cuts don't pay.
- H1.4: augmentation (E008).
- H2.3: selective backprop (E012).
- H6.1: LR to zero (E015).
- H2.1.2 (E013) and H2.5/H2.5.1 (E014).

Corrections:
- H2.5 was rewritten: E006 never used random-resized crop, so only the 2x2 final-map half was tested (and refuted), and the crop half is retired as moot. H2.1's wording was fixed the same way.
- H2.6 was corrected: group 2, not group 1, carries ~48% of the FLOPs.
- H1.5.1 is supported by E007.
- H5 was trimmed to 0.55; it rests on external evidence only.
- H6 was narrowed to regime-specific levers.

New nodes:
- N1/N1a: total epochs matter more than the 32 px share; a 24 px epoch substitutes for most of a 32 px one.
- N2: 24->32 two-stage schedule at 9.5-10 epochs, with no 28 px phase. This is the next run to do.
- N3/N3a: resolutions below 24 px.
- N4/N4a: smaller batches for accuracy at equal time.
- N5/N5a: tanh-approximate GELU.
- N6: epoch slope above 8.5 epochs.

Open housekeeping:
- Report E013/E016's augmentation hashes to close H2.1.3.
- E006's results.tsv description wrongly says random-resized crop; per its implementation note, it used flip + translate followed by an antialiased downsample.
